plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 4: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
plan.contextChunk: This figure presents a single labeled sketch of a logistic growth curve on unscaled axes: a horizontal axis labeled t and a vertical axis labeled f(t), both double-arrowed and carrying no numeric ticks. A dashed orange horizontal line stretches across the upper part of the plot, tagged y = c at its left end and joined by a black leader to the annotation Carrying capacity. The solid dark blue curve enters from the lower left, crosses the vertical axis at a marked point labeled (0, c/(1 + a)) and identified as the Initial value of population, steepens through the middle of the frame, then flattens and runs rightward just beneath the dashed line without meeting it. A filled dot on the steepest part of the rise is labeled with the coordinates (ln(a)/b, c/2) and connected by a leader to the words Point of maximum growth. The curve's formula, f(t) = c/(1 + ae^(-bx)), is printed in blue to the right of the upper bend. The three annotations single out what the reader is meant to take from the shape: where the curve starts, where its slope is greatest, and the ceiling it approaches. Together they establish that growth of this kind accelerates only until the population reaches half the carrying capacity, after which the rate of increase falls away as the curve saturates.

interactionPlan.concept: A logistic growth curve increases most rapidly when it reaches half its carrying capacity, then slows as it approaches the horizontal asymptote y = c.

vertical f(t)-axis with arrowheads at both ends and label f(t) at the top
solid dark blue logistic growth curve f(t) = c/(1 + ae^(-bt)) rising in an S-shape from lower left to upper right
orange dashed horizontal carrying-capacity line y = c across the upper plot
orange label y = c at the left end of the dashed line
black leader line from the dashed line to the annotation 'Carrying capacity'
filled dark blue point on the vertical axis marking the initial value
coordinate label (0, c/(1 + a)) beside the initial point
black leader line from the initial point to the annotation 'Initial value of population'
filled dark blue point at the inflection point on the steepest part of the curve
coordinate label (ln(a)/b, c/2) beside the inflection point
black leader line from the inflection point to the annotation 'Point of maximum growth'
blue formula label f(t) = c/(1 + ae^(-bt)) near the upper right part of the curve
movable dark blue time marker on the logistic curve
short tangent line through the movable time marker showing instantaneous slope
vertical gap indicator from the movable point up to the dashed line y = c showing distance below carrying capacity
dynamic readout for current time t, population f(t), tangent slope, and remaining gap c - f(t)

interactions.label: Time t
interactions.teaches: As time advances, the population first accelerates, reaches its fastest growth at f(t) = c/2, and then slows because the remaining distance to carrying capacity shrinks

interactions.label: Growth rate b
interactions.teaches: Increasing b makes the transition from low population to near carrying capacity sharper and moves the maximum-growth time ln(a)/b closer to the start

demo_steps.title: Start below the carrying capacity
demo_steps.narration: At early times, the curve is low and the population is still far below y = c. The tangent slope is small, so growth has not yet reached its fastest phase.

demo_steps.title: Find the fastest growth point
demo_steps.narration: Drag t to the labeled point (ln(a)/b, c/2). The tangent is steepest here, showing that logistic growth is fastest when the population is exactly half of the carrying capacity.

demo_steps.title: Approach saturation
demo_steps.narration: As t moves farther right, the curve flattens beneath the dashed line y = c. The population is still increasing, but the tangent slope and remaining gap both shrink.

demo_steps.title: Change the growth rate
demo_steps.narration: Increasing b makes the S-curve steeper and shifts the maximum-growth point left, so the population moves through its rapid-growth phase sooner and more abruptly.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: In logistic growth, the maximum growth rate occurs at the inflection point f(t) = c/2, not when the population is small or when it is near carrying capacity.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a clean unscaled coordinate sketch rather than numeric axes. The logistic curve should be dark blue, thick, and S-shaped, crossing the vertical axis at the labeled initial value and leveling off just below the orange dashed carrying-capacity line. Keep the carrying-capacity label and maximum-growth label prominent with black leader lines. For the interactive overlay, place a movable marker directly on the curve, draw a small tangent segment at that point, and show a vertical dashed or bracketed gap up to y = c. Use normalized internal values such as c = 1 and a = 4 for plotting while preserving the symbolic labels shown in the original figure.

authoredContext:
The graph in the figure shows how the growth rate changes over time. The graph increases from left to right, but the growth rate only increases until it reaches its point of maximum growth rate, at which point the rate of increase decreases.

Graph of f(t)=c/(1+ae^(-tx)). The carrying capacity is the asymptote at y=c. The initial value of population is (0, c/(1+a)). The point of maximum growth is (ln(a)/b, c/2).

discrepancies: The generated default view adds a movable highlighted marker, tangent segment, vertical dashed guide to y=c, and numerical readout box that are not in the source figure and visually clutter the static textbook composition.
The blue logistic curve lacks the arrowheads at its left and right ends that appear in the source figure.
The vertical dashed guide at t=0 overlays the y-axis in the default state, making the axis look partly blue/dashed rather than a clean black axis as in the source.
The top f(t) axis label is clipped at the top edge in the screenshot, reducing legibility compared with the fully visible source label.
The coordinate labels are rendered as crude two-line text approximations rather than clean stacked fractions, and the point-of-maximum-growth area is crowded by the added readout/tangent annotations.
evaluation.notes: The main logistic curve, carrying-capacity line, axes, and key labeled points are conceptually correct and recognizable, but the default state is cluttered by extra interactive annotations and has some label/arrowhead fidelity problems.
action_items: Hide the movable marker, tangent line, vertical guide, and numeric readout in the default static state, or make them appear only after interaction/demo steps.
Add small blue arrowheads to both ends of the logistic curve to match the source.
Move the f(t) label downward or increase top padding so it is not clipped.
Improve the fraction-style coordinate and equation labels so they more closely resemble the source and avoid crowding near the inflection-point annotation.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interactivity are correct, but the remaining issues are implementation-level fidelity fixes such as hiding extra default annotations, adding curve arrowheads, improving padding, and refining labels.
